references.text: The same chapter describes that a house with leprosy must be torn down, and the stones, timber, and all the mortar shall be taken to an unclean place outside the city.
The person with leprosy was to live outside the camp, separated from the community, reflecting the principle of removing uncleanness to a place outside.
Unclean persons, including those with leprosy, were to be sent outside the camp so as not to defile it.
Moses exhorts the people to carefully follow the priests' instructions regarding leprosy, just as the priest gives this command here.
The introduction to the laws concerning leprosy in houses, where the homeowner must report a possible outbreak to the priest.
Jesus suffered outside the city gate to sanctify the people, which can be seen as a fulfillment of carrying uncleanness outside the camp.
